facts.statement: Nodosaurus is a genus of herbivorous ankylosaurian dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous found only in the Frontier Formation of Wyoming.
facts.quote: Nodosaurus (meaning 'knobbed lizard') is a genus of herbivorous nodosaurid ankylosaurian dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous, the fossils of which are found exclusively in the Frontier Formation in Wyoming.

facts.statement: Fossils of Nodosaurus were first discovered on July 17, 1881, by collector William Harlow Reed in Albany County, Wyoming.
facts.quote: Fossils of Nodosaurus were first discovered on 17 July, 1881 by fossil collector William Harlow Reed in Albany County, Wyoming in the western United States.

facts.statement: Othniel Charles Marsh scientifically described Nodosaurus and named the species Nodosaurus textilis in 1889.
facts.quote: In 1889, Othniel Charles Marsh scientifically described the remains and assigned them to a new genus and species of ornithischian dinosaur, which he named Nodosaurus textilis.

facts.statement: Nodosaurus grew to roughly 4 to 6 meters long and had bony dermal plates covering its body, possibly with spikes along its sides.
facts.quote: Nodosaurus grew up to roughly 4 to 6 m long and it was an ornithischian dinosaur with bony dermal plates covering the top of its body, and it may have had spikes along its side as well.

facts.statement: A 2010 estimate by Paul suggests Nodosaurus reached a length of 6 meters and a weight of 3.5 tonnes.
facts.quote: In 2010 Paul estimated its length at 6 meters (20 ft) and its weight at 3.5 tonnes (3.85 short tons).

facts.statement: Nodosaurus likely ate soft plants due to its inability to chew tough fibrous ones, or it may have processed tough plants using gastroliths and a large intestinal apparatus.
facts.quote: It perhaps ate soft plants, as it would have been unable to chew tough, fibrous ones; or alternatively it may have processed the latter with gastroliths and its enormous intestinal apparatus.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest that without a tail club, Nodosaurus likely defended itself by rolling onto its back to expose only its armored sides and rear, similar to modern hedgehogs.
facts.quote: Se piensa que sin una maza en su cola, 'Nodosaurus' ' no habría tenido mucho en términos de defensas activas. Cuando estaba amenazado, probablemente se echaba a la tierra de modo que solamente su parte posterior y lados acorazados quedaban expuestos, como en los modernos erizos.

facts.statement: The unique variation in the arrangement of osteoderm rows on the posterior body is known to be exclusive to Nodosaurus.
facts.quote: La extraña variación en la forma de las filas de osteodermos en la parte posterior a menudo ha sido imitada por ilustraciones de otros anquilosaurios, pero se sabe que es exclusiva de Nodosaurus.

facts.statement: Nodosaurus belongs to the subfamily Nodosaurinae within the family Nodosauridae.
facts.quote: Within Nodosauridae, Nodosaurus falls out in the subfamily Nodosaurinae, formally defined as the largest clade containing Nodosaurus textilis but not Hylaeosaurus armatus, Mymoorapelta maysi and Polacanthus foxii.

facts.statement: It is debated whether the nodosaurids Stegopelta and Hierosaurus are synonyms of Nodosaurus, a hypothesis proposed in 1978 that has received little support.
facts.quote: Later in 1978, paleontologist Walter Coombs Jr. hypothesized that the other nodosaurids Stegopelta and Hierosaurus were synonyms of Nodosaurus, but this has seen little support.

facts.statement: Nodosaurus is known from two incomplete fossil specimens that lack skulls.
facts.quote: Es conocido por dos especímenes fósiles incompletos descubiertos, a los que le falta el cráneo.

facts.statement: One of the known specimens was found in the Thermopolis Shale of Wyoming.
facts.quote: Uno encontrado en la Pizarra Thermopolis de Wyoming.

facts.statement: A third specimen is believed to exist in Mexico, but it has not been confirmed as Nodosaurus.
facts.quote: Se cree que hay un tercero en México pero no se ha confirmado que sea un Nodosaurus.

facts.statement: The genus was named by Othniel Charles Marsh in 1889.
facts.quote: siendo nombrado por Othniel Charles Marsh en 1889

facts.statement: The genus name means "knotted lizard" in Latin, referring to the bumps on the leg armor.
facts.quote: El nombre del género significa "lagarto nudoso" del latín nodus , "nudo, botón" y se refiere a las protuberancias de la armadura de las piernas.

facts.statement: The species name means "braided" in Latin, referring to the pattern of the armor.
facts.quote: La designación de especie significa "trenzado" en latín y se refiere al patrón de la armadura.

facts.statement: The holotype, YPM 1815, was found in the Belle Fourche Member of the Frontier Formation.
facts.quote: El holotipo, YPM 1815, se encontró en el miembro Belle Fourche, un depósito marino de la formación Frontier

facts.statement: The holotype dates to the middle Cenomanian, approximately 97 million years ago.
facts.quote: que se remonta al Cenomaniense medio y tiene aproximadamente 97 millones de años.

facts.statement: The dating of Nodosaurus has also been given as the Albian.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, la datación de Nodosaurus también se ha dado como del Albiense.

facts.statement: The genus was well described by Lull in 1921 based on partial skeletal remains.
facts.quote: bien descrito por Llul en 1921 a partir de restos parciales de un esqueleto.

facts.statement: The holotype consists of a partial skeleton without a skull.
facts.quote: El holotipo consiste en un esqueleto parcial sin cráneo.

facts.statement: The holotype preserves three back vertebrae, thirteen tail vertebrae, a sacrum, ribs, parts of a scapula, humerus, left elbow and radius, metacarpals, phalanges, both ilia, a left femur, both tibiae, a left perone piece, a left foot, parts of the posterior dorsal armor, a left hip shield, a keeled osteoderm, a vertebral column, and a column-shaped plate.
facts.quote: Se han conservado los siguientes elementos, tres vértebras de la espalda, trece vértebras de la cola, un sacro, costillas, la parte superior de un omóplato, piezas de un húmero, piezas de codo izquierdo y radio izquierdo, huesos metacarpianos, falanges, ambos huesos ilíacos, un fémur izquierdo, ambas tibias, una pieza de peroné izquierdo, el pie izquierdo, la parte izquierda de la armadura dorsal posterior, la parte izquierda de un escudo de cadera, un osteodermo con quilla, una columna vertebral y una placa en forma de columna.

facts.statement: No other findings have been assigned to the species except for some loose armor plates.
facts.quote: Nunca se han asignado otros hallazgos a la especie, excepto algunas placas de armadura sueltas.

facts.statement: The material was described again by Richard Swann Lull in 1921.
facts.quote: En 1921 el material fue descrito nuevamente por Richard Swann Lull.

facts.statement: The reconstruction in the publication was the first published reconstruction of a nodosaurid.
facts.quote: La reconstrucción en la publicación fue la primera que se publicó a de un nodosáurido.

facts.statement: In 1978, Walter Preston Coombs renamed taxa as Nodosaurus species, creating Nodosaurus sternbergi and Nodosaurus coleii.
facts.quote: En 1978, Walter Preston Coombs renombró a los taxones como especies de Nodosaurus, produciendo un Nodosaurus sternbergi y un Nodosaurus coleii.

facts.statement: Coombs also renamed Stegopelta as Nodosaurus landerensis in 1978, but the name Stegopelta is generally used today.
facts.quote: Coombs también renombró Stegopelta en 1978 como Nodosaurus landerensis, hoy en día, sin embargo, el nombre Stegopelta se usa generalmente.

facts.statement: Marsh originally placed Nodosaurus within Stegosauria in 1889.
facts.quote: En 1889, Marsh colocó originalmente a Nodosaurus dentro de Stegosauria.

facts.statement: In 1890 Marsh named his own family Nodosauridae but thought they were part of the Ceratopsia.
facts.quote: En 1890 nombró a su propia familia Nodosauridae, pero pensó que eran parte de la Ceratopsia.

facts.statement: In 1896 Marsh returned Nodosaurus to Stegosauria along with various other armored species.
facts.quote: En 1896, Marsh devolvió a Nodosaurus a Stegosauria, junto con todo tipo de otras especies blindadas.

facts.statement: Nodosaurus is the homonym of Nodosauridae, one of the two subgroups of Ankylosauria, and is found in this group in most studies.
facts.quote: Nodosaurus es el homónimo de Nodosauridae, uno de los dos subgrupos de Ankylosauria y se encuentra en este grupo en la mayoría de los estudios.

facts.statement: Vickaryous et al. in 2004 found the findings too scarce for exact classification and listed them as "Ankylosauria incertae sedis".
facts.quote: Vickaryous, M. y col. en 2004, sin embargo, encuentran los hallazgos demasiado escasos para una clasificación exacta y los enumeran como "Ankylosauria incertae sedis".

facts.statement: The time range for Nodosaurus is from the Cenomanian to the Maastrichtian (100.5 to 66 million years ago).
facts.quote: Time range: Cenomanian to Maastrichtian (100.5 to 66 million years ago)

facts.statement: The parent group of Nodosaurus is Nodosauridae.
facts.quote: Parent group: Nodosauridae

facts.statement: The family of Nodosaurus is Nodosauridae.
facts.quote: Family: Nodosauridae

facts.statement: The class of Nodosaurus is Ornithischia.
facts.quote: Class: Ornithischia

facts.statement: The type species of Nodosaurus is Nodosaurus textilis.
facts.quote: Type species: Nodosaurus textilis

rejected.quote: Nodosaurus textilis es la única especie conocida del género extinto Nodosaurus ... que vivió a finales del período Cretácico, entre 100 a 97 millones de años atrás, durante el Cenomaniense en lo que hoy es Norteamérica.

rejected.quote: Nodosaurus es uno de los primeros dinosaurios acorazados descubiertos en Estados Unidos
